conversation.message: The Earth's rotation is a remnant of the angular momentum from the collapsing cloud of gas and dust that formed our solar system. This initial spin has been conserved over billions of years.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: A faster rotation would slightly reduce the effective gravity at the equator due to increased centrifugal force, but it wouldn't significantly change the actual gravitational pull of the Earth.
